cards.body:
## Summary
The LT driver judges Linga through a text copy of the screens that it writes by hand. That copy has drifted from the real TV and phone four times, and each drift turned into findings that were not true: a theme that had to be refuted, a recap gap carried as 'still open', a phone situation picker the Characters never saw, and a verdict with its evidence missing. This card makes the driver render the real LingaTV and LingaPhone components (react-dom/server, in-process, as the rules suites already load desk TS) and read their text and controls. From then on a drift is a failing test or a counted line in the run report, not something found in a verification pass later.

## Description
uat/driver/surface.cjs exports surfaceOf(session) -> {screen, shown, heard, offered, unmapped}. `shown` is the text of renderToStaticMarkup(LingaTV) and renderToStaticMarkup(LingaPhone) for the session, in TV and Phone sections, with collapsed <details> marked as tap-to-open. `heard` is the one audio channel no markup carries: the question, listen line or partner line the TV speaks. `offered` comes from one table: each row is an action id, the rendered control labels it matches, what it needs (text/option/band/topicId/sceneId) and the englishCommand it sends. An action is offered only when its control is in this render. Rendered controls with no row are returned as `unmapped` and counted in report.md under 'Driver coverage'. linga-text.cjs loses surface(), run() and ACTIONS (about 97 lines) and gains a .tsx require hook (jsx: react-jsx). judgePayload() stops cutting screens silently. No product file changes, so the TV gate does not apply.

## Flow
- child() builds the session as today, then each step calls surfaceOf(getSession()) instead of the closure
- The Character sees TV and phone text as the components render it, plus the heard line
- The chosen action runs through the table's command. A choice with no rendered control is recorded as 'not-offered', as today
- report.md gains one line: unmapped controls per screen (0 is the target) and not-offered picks
- The judge reads each step whole, or with an explicit cut marker

## Expected impact
This removes the class of finding that the operator had to refute or scope by hand: 13 in run 1 and 13 of 24 recap findings across three runs. The phone's first-visit situation picker becomes visible to the Characters. That is a real product question, where the driver hides it today. The next /uat drain then starts from findings the screens actually support. Driver changes get a gate beyond node --check.

## Evaluation
Claim: the driver's view of each Linga screen is derived from the rendered components, and every drift is a failing test or a counted report line
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (surface() is a closure inside child() and cannot be imported. 4 drifts are documented, 13 of 24 recap findings were driver-blind, and the judge's cut is silent)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

cards.body:
## Summary
Closing the loop after a Linga fix takes the operator about five manual steps. They pick which Characters and journeys to rerun, launch a fresh run, read two reports side by side, type the before/after metrics, reason out confounds, and edit findings.json and recertify.md by hand. It has been done three times, and the /uat skill's own contract (rerun only the affected pairs, write resolutions back into the originating run, carry prior ids and recurrence) has never been met. `node uat/driver/linga-text.cjs --recertify 2026-09-15-lt-recert2-beginners` makes it one command. The run already holds the data; this card makes the driver read it.

## Description
uat/driver/recertify.cjs is a pure module over run directories. plan(prior) returns the Character x journey pairs with open non-strength findings. metricDelta(before, after) recomputes the rubric metrics from each run's per-Character JSON. confounds(before, after) flags a different journey start (real vs fixture, from `setup`), a different journey set, and a different instrument (a new run.json with driver sha256, model, efforts and judge screen cap). writeBack(prior, statuses) stamps the originating findings.json: not-seen -> 'fixed' (LT never claims 'resolved-verified'), recurs -> recurrence+1, missing -> 'not-evaluable'. renderRecertify() writes recertify.md beside the originating run, in the shape the operator already writes by hand. linga-text.cjs gains --recertify <id>. It runs plan()'s pairs, and each judge call gets that pair's prior findings with a required prior[] {id, status, evidence} in the schema. It also writes run.json on every run.

## Flow
- The operator lands a fix, then runs `--recertify <run>`
- The driver reruns only the open pairs (7 for the beginners run, where all 10 Characters were rerun before)
- The judge marks each prior id recurs / not-seen with step evidence
- The originating findings.json is stamped, and recertify.md is written beside it with fixed / still open / regressed / deltas / confounds / new findings
- /uat drain reads one table, not three documents

## Expected impact
The fix -> proof cycle drops from a hand-written document to one command, at a fraction of the codex calls (7 pairs, where a full re-cast is 10 Characters x 2-4 journeys). Confounds like the 52% -> 34% topic-fit scare are flagged before anyone reads them as a regression. Recurrence becomes real, so an issue that keeps coming back outranks a new one, as the skill intends. Every run records its instrument, so a driver change such as the judge cut can no longer look like a product change.

## Evaluation
Claim: a recertification is one command whose output meets the skill's recertify contract and reproduces, from data, the numbers and confounds the operator has worked out by hand
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (no module and no flag. 190 recertification findings with 0 recurrence > 1 and 0 written back)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: none
